prompt:
You are the Argus Retro eye, judging SCOPE DRIFT inside a ticket.
Each block below is work done in a session registered to a ticket,
together with what that ticket actually asked for. For each block answer
ONE question: is this diff what the ticket asked for?
Do not run any commands; judge only from the blocks.

## The policy — read it before you answer

The burden of proof is on DRIFT. Report drift ONLY for work that serves a
DIFFERENT goal than the ticket states. All of the following are IN scope
and are NOT drift, even when the ticket never mentions them:

- refactors of the code the ticket touches, however large;
- test additions, test updates and fixtures for the ticket's work;
- renames, moves, formatting and type-level cleanup along the way;
- anything the stated work depends on, including changes to other files;
- fixing something that was blocking the build, the tests or the gates.

If a diff is a plausible way to accomplish the stated scope, it is NOT
drift. If you are unsure, it is NOT drift: set drift false, or leave
confident false. Ambiguity resolves to silence.

This asymmetry is deliberate. One false positive costs Johan's trust in
every retro issue Argus will ever file; one missed drift costs a single
un-filed issue. When the two are balanced, choose silence.

Evidence may have been truncated to fit this prompt. Truncation is NOT
evidence of drift — judge only what you can actually see.

Emit JSON matching the output schema, one entry per candidate id:
- drift: true only for work serving a different goal than the ticket states.
- confident: false whenever you are unsure; an unsure drift is not reported.
- what: a short phrase naming the out-of-scope work, or null.
- outOfScopeWork: what was done that the ticket did not ask for,
  concretely — files and behaviour — or null.
- whyOutOfScope: why it serves a different goal, or null.

ticket: #50 provenance: a real headless Claude prompt carries promptSource sdk and is not a candidate, so dispatch provenance is lost
stated scope:
**Found by [#49](https://github.com/JohanSardar/argus/issues/49)'s live Opus 5 drive — the first time `src/tailing/claude-code.ts` ever met a real transcript. Reported, deliberately not fixed there: it is a policy question, not a parser bug.**

## The finding

A real `claude -p` prompt carries `promptSource: "sdk"`. The candidate filter accepts `typed` and `queued`. `sdk` is neither — so a Hermes dispatch into a headless Claude session lands as **`system` / `non-candidate`** instead of **`hermes` / `dispatch-prompt`**, and the dispatch provenance is lost.

**This has a live consequence today:** [#43](https://github.com/JohanSardar/argus/issues/43)'s Claude drive asserts `via === "dispatch-prompt"`. With the token gate removed by #49, that assertion **would fail on a real headless transcript**. It has never run, so it has never failed.

**The sharpest part of the finding** is that the *same logical event* — Hermes dispatching a worker — is recorded differently depending only on how the session was opened:

| how the session opened | `promptSource` | classified |
|---|---|---|
| terminal / TUI (15 records observed) | `typed` | `hermes` / `dispatch-prompt` ✅ |
| headless `claude -p` (10 records observed) | `sdk` | `system` / `non-candidate` ❌ |

Argus's own dispatcher spawns workers **headlessly**, so this is the path Argus uses on itself.

It fails **safe** — deafness, never poisoning: a dispatch is dropped, never misattributed to Johan. But losing dispatch provenance is a §5 gap.

Also observed and worth recording: **`promptSource: "queued"` never appears in 18,000 lines of real transcripts.** The filter accepts it; nothing produces it. Unexercised, not wrong — but do not assume it is load-bearing.

## Scope

1. Decide the policy: is an `sdk`-sourced prompt a candidate? Argue it from §5 provenance, not from what is convenient for the tests. The registry-match path is what actually establishes "this was Hermes", so consider whether `promptSource` should gate candidacy at all, or whether the matcher should be the authority with `promptSource` as evidence rather than a filter.
2. Implement the decision with a red test first, pinning the **real** shape (`sdk`, headless) rather than a hand-written fixture — that is the exact class of blindness #49 and [#42](https://github.com/JohanSardar/argus/issues/42) both found.
3. **Fix or re-point #43's `via === "dispatch-prompt"` assertion** so it is true of a real headless transcript, and say which.
4. If `queued` is genuinely unreachable, say so in a comment in the code rather than silently keeping it.

## Hard rules

Temp dirs and sandbox slugs only. Never touch real `~/.claude` state beyond **read-only** transcript reads, and never `~/.claude/.credentials.json`. Never run `setup-token`, `/login`, `logout`, `claude auth`. Never kill a process this ticket did not spawn. Gates: `bun x tsc --noEmit` + `bun test` green, zero runtime dependencies.

+# Real headless Claude Code transcript lines (ticket #50)
+
+Every line in this directory is **verbatim bytes from a real transcript** on the
+machine that ran #49's live drive — copied, never composed. Nothing was
+rewritten, reordered or pretty-printed; the only editing is *omission* of whole
+records the parser ignores anyway (`attachment`, `last-prompt`, `atis-latch`).
+
+That is the point of the directory. Every other Claude fixture in this tree is
+hand-written, and hand-written input is the exact blindness #36, #42 and #49
+each found the hard way: a fixture only contains the fields whoever wrote it
+already knew about. These files carry the sixteen fields a real record has —
+`promptSource`, `origin`, `entrypoint`, `promptId`, `permissionMode`,
+`userType`, `gitBranch`, `version` — because a real CLI wrote them.
+
+They live in their own directory, not in `../claude-code/`, because
+`src/tailing/replay.test.ts` replays that whole directory and pins its event
+stream by exact equality.
+
+## `argus-49-drive.jsonl`
+
+Lines 1, 2, 4 and 12 of
+`~/.claude/projects/-private-var-…-argus-harness-wBOI80-worktrees-live-subscription/c9cfecd3-2e6e-4a89-8b4f-11537f94cdda.jsonl`
+— the transcript **#49's own subscription drive produced** (Claude Opus 5,
+`claude -p`, CLI 2.1.246). Argus's own output end to end, so there is nothing
+private in it.
+
+- two `queue-operation` openers with a `sessionId` and **no `cwd`** — the shape
+  that made #49 fix the `session-meta` latch;
+- the dispatch prompt: `promptSource: "sdk"`, `entrypoint: "sdk-cli"`, **no
+  `origin`** — the record this whole ticket is about;
+- the assistant's reply.
+
+## `task-notification.jsonl`
+
+Lines 668 and 727 of
+`~/.claude/projects/-Users-johansardar-argus-worktrees-acceptance/42659fbd-2f38-4bfe-bb06-a883bcea2492.jsonl`
+— an Argus build worker's own session (CLI 2.1.245).
+
+- a real assistant turn, which closes the session's opening run;
+- a real `<task-notification>` **injected as a user-role record** with
+  `promptSource: "sdk"` and `origin.kind: "task-notification"`, at line 727 of
+  792: deep mid-session, hundreds of records past any preamble window.
+
+This is the poisoning direction, and it is why #50's fix is not "add `sdk` to
+the allowlist". Measured across 60 project slugs / 234 transcripts / 340,222
+lines on this machine: **34 of 34** `sdk`-sourced `<task-notification>` records
+arrive mid-session, so #42's envelope-plus-opening-run rule would have caught
+**zero** of them and every one would have landed in USER.md as Johan.

+/**
+ * Ticket #50 — the same records, but REAL ones.
+ *
+ * Everything above is hand-written, and hand-written input is what #36, #42
+ * and #49 each got caught by: a fixture carries the fields its author already
+ * knew about. The records below are verbatim lines from real transcripts
+ * (`tests/fixtures/claude-code-headless/README.md` names the file and line of
+ * each), so they carry the sixteen fields a real record has — including the
+ * two this ticket turns on, `promptSource` and `origin`.
+ *
+ * The population behind the numbers quoted here: 60 project slugs, 234
+ * transcripts, 340,222 lines, 59,816 `type: "user"` records on this machine,
+ * run through this function.
+ */
+const headlessFixtures = fileURLToPath(
+  new URL("../../tests/fixtures/claude-code-headless/", import.meta.url),
+);
+
+async function realRecords(file: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]> {
+  const text = await readFile(join(headlessFixtures, file), "utf8");
+  return text
+    .split("\n")
+    .filter((line) => line.trim() !== "")
+    .map((line) => JSON.parse(line) as Record<string, unknown>);
+}
+
+const content = (record: Record<string, unknown>): string =>
+  (record.message as { content: string }).content;
+
+describe("claudeCandidateText on REAL headless records (#50)", () => {
+  test("a real `claude -p` dispatch prompt is a candidate", async () => {
+    const [dispatch] = (await realRecords("argus-49-drive.jsonl")).filter(
+      (record) => record.type === "user",
+    );
+
+    // The shape first, so a CLI change that moves the goalposts fails HERE
+    // rather than silently making the assertion below vacuous.
+    expect({
+      promptSource: dispatch!.promptSource,
+      entrypoint: dispatch!.entrypoint,
+      origin: dispatch!.origin,
+    }).toEqual({ promptSource: "sdk", entrypoint: "sdk-cli", origin: undefined });
+
+    expect(claudeCandidateText(dispatch)).toBe(content(dispatch!));
+  });
+
+  // The sharpest half of #50: the SAME logical event — Hermes dispatching a
+  // worker — is `typed` when the session was opened in a terminal and `sdk`
+  // when it was opened headlessly. Argus's own dispatcher spawns every worker
+  // headlessly, so `sdk` is the path Argus takes on itself. How a session was
+  // opened is not provenance, and candidacy must not read it as if it were.
+  test("the same record differs only by how the session was opened", async () => {
+    const [dispatch] = (await realRecords("argus-49-drive.jsonl")).filter(
+      (record) => record.type === "user",
+    );
+    const typedInATerminal = { ...dispatch, promptSource: "typed" };
+
+    expect(claudeCandidateText(typedInATerminal)).toBe(
+      claudeCandidateText(dispatch),
+    );
+  });
+
+  // The poisoning direction, and the reason the fix is NOT "add sdk to the
+  // allowlist". This record is real, `sdk`-sourced, and sits at line 727 of a
+  // 792-line session: #42's envelope-plus-opening-run rule cannot see it.
+  // Measured: 34 of 34 sdk `<task-notification>` records arrive mid-session.
+  test("a real mid-session <task-notification> is refused", async () => {
+    const [notification] = (await realRecords("task-notification.jsonl")).filter(
+      (record) => record.type === "user",
+    );
+
+    expect({
+      promptSource: notification!.promptSource,
+      origin: notification!.origin,
+    }).toEqual({ promptSource: "sdk", origin: { kind: "task-notification" } });
+    expect(claudeCandidateText(notification)).toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  test("...and it is `origin` that refuses it, not the shape or the position", async () => {
+    const [notification] = (await realRecords("task-notification.jsonl")).filter(
+      (record) => record.type === "user",
+    );
+    const { origin: _drop, ...withoutOrigin } = notification!;
+
+    // Same bytes, same envelope shape, same mid-session position — the only
+    // thing removed is the CLI's own statement of what the record is. If that
+    // is what flips the verdict, `origin` is doing the work.
+    expect(claudeCandidateText(withoutOrigin)).toBe(content(notification!));
+    expect(syntheticEnvelopeTag(content(notification!))).toBe("task-notification");
+  });
+
+  // 162 real records on this machine: Johan typing into the Claude desktop
+  // app, which fronts the SDK. Dropping these is the deafness direction —
+  // USER.md never learns from a word he says in that app (§13.4 the other way
+  // round, and silent, which is worse).
+  test("a desktop prompt marked `origin: human` is a candidate", async () => {
+    const [dispatch] = (await realRecords("argus-49-drive.jsonl")).filter(
+      (record) => record.type === "user",
+    );
+    const desktop = {
+      ...dispatch,
+      entrypoint: "claude-desktop",
+      origin: { kind: "human" },
+      message: { role: "user", content: "confirm" },
+    };
+
+    expect(claudeCandidateText(desktop)).toBe("confirm");
+  });
+
+  // Observed once, verbatim: Johan accepting a suggestion, text "yes agreed".
+  // An allowlist is silent about what it has never heard of; this is what that
+  // silence costs, and it is why unknown SOURCE names default open.
+  test("a promptSource the filter has never seen is still heard", async () => {
+    const [dispatch] = (await realRecords("argus-49-drive.jsonl")).filter(
+      (record) => record.type === "user",
+    );
+
+    expect(
+      claudeCandidateText({
+        ...dispatch,
+        promptSource: "suggestion_accepted",
+        origin: { kind: "human" },
+        message: { role: "user", content: "yes agreed" },
+      }),
+    ).toBe("yes agreed");
+  });
+
+  // The other default, and it points the other way ON PURPOSE: an origin kind
+  // the CLI invents later is content the CLI is telling us it produced, so it
+  // is refused until someone looks. Adding injection kinds is the thing CLIs
+  // actually do (#36's `<recommended_plugins>` was exactly that).
+  test("an origin kind nobody has seen yet is refused", async () => {
+    const [dispatch] = (await realRecords("argus-49-drive.jsonl")).filter(
+      (record) => record.type === "user",
+    );
+
+    expect(
+      claudeCandidateText({ ...dispatch, origin: { kind: "hook-result" } }),
+    ).toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  test("promptSource `system` — the CLI's own marker — is still refused", async () => {
+    const [dispatch] = (await realRecords("argus-49-drive.jsonl")).filter(
+      (record) => record.type === "user",
+    );
+
+    // 612 records on this machine carry it; 612 of them are task-notifications
+    // and none is a prompt anybody sent.
+    expect(claudeCandidateText({ ...dispatch, promptSource: "system" })).toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  // #50's ticket says `queued` "never appears in 18,000 lines of real
+  // transcripts" and asks whether it is reachable. It is: #49 surveyed the
+  // `*argus*` slugs only. Across all 60 slugs on this machine `queued` appears
+  // 110 times in string-content non-meta user records. Reachable, exercised,
+  // and not to be removed.
+  test("`queued` is reachable in real data, not a dead branch", async () => {
+    const [dispatch] = (await realRecords("argus-49-drive.jsonl")).filter(
+      (record) => record.type === "user",
+    );
+
+    expect(claudeCandidateText({ ...dispatch, promptSource: "queued" })).toBe(
+      content(dispatch!),
+    );
+  });
+});
